findings.title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: File app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 interpolates <%= request.referer %> directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string without JavaScript escaping. Referer is a fully attacker-controlled request header, so a value containing ' can break out and inject arbitrary script executed in the forum origin. Additionally the full referer URL (with path/query) is used as postMessage targetOrigin, which must be an origin; this breaks delivery and encourages a wildcard fix.

findings.title: Stored XSS via unsanitized RSS/remote HTML stored as raw_html
findings.body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13 appends an unsanitized link built from feed-controlled url ("#{url}") and TopicEmbed.import stores feed/readability HTML verbatim with cook_method raw_html. Combined with app/models/post.rb bypass that returns raw without sanitization and app/views/embed/best.html.erb using raw post.cooked, an attacker who controls feed content or linked page content gets persistent script execution in forum and embedded contexts. absolutize_urls only rewrites leading-/ URLs and leaves script tags, event handlers, and javascript: URLs intact.

findings.title: raw_html cook_method bypasses sanitization pipeline
findings.body: File app/models/post.rb line 133 in Post#cook returns raw directly when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking/sanitization and plugin filters. Any raw_html post content (from RSS polling or readability fetch) is then stored as cooked and rendered with raw in views, so unsanitized external HTML becomes stored XSS across topic pages, not just the embed iframe.

findings.title: Reversed postMessage origin check accepts prefix origins
findings.body: File app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17 checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 instead of checking that e.origin equals the expected Discourse origin. This tests whether the attacker-controlled origin is a substring of the trusted URL, so any origin that happens to be a string prefix of discourseUrl would be accepted and can drive iframe resizing. Origin validation must be strict equality against the expected origin.

findings.title: import_remote uses open without open-uri, enabling local file read
findings.body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48 calls open(url).read without requiring open-uri. When called via Jobs::RetrieveTopic / TopicRetriever (which never requires open-uri), Kernel#open treats the argument as a file path, so fetching fails for HTTP and can read local files. It also has no timeout, redirect limit, size limit, or error handling, allowing SSRF, hangs, and job crashes.

findings.title: Feed polling crashes on nil content and leaks resources with unbounded work
findings.body: File app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29 does SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no rescue, timeout, or close, and line 35 does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without nil guards for content/title/link. A single malformed item, network error, huge feed, or missing field raises NoMethodError or network exception and aborts the hourly job, while iterating every item each hour can create unbounded topics.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx plus expire throttle can permanently block retrieval
findings.body: File lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-28 implements the 60-second retrieval throttle as $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires, so that embed_url is throttled forever. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX (or setex) and normalize/hash the URL for the key.

findings.title: Race on embed creation and wrong persisted check can raise duplicate key
findings.body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 20-28 checks embed.blank? then creates Topic/Post/TopicEmbed without handling concurrent creators. Two concurrent retrieve/poll jobs for the same embed_url both pass the check and the second hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url with RecordNotUnique. Also the guard uses post.present? instead of post.persisted?, so a failed PostCreator result with errors still attempts TopicEmbed.create! with nil ids.

findings.title: content_sha1 updated even when revision fails or post is missing
findings.body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 32-37 calls PostRevisor#revise! without checking its false return value or whether embed.post is nil (e.g., deleted post), then unconditionally does embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1). A failed or skipped revision permanently marks the new content as synced, so legitimate feed changes are never retried.

findings.title: Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header will not allow framing
findings.body: File app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 28 sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] to ALLOWALL to permit iframing. ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive and browsers ignore or treat it as deny; to allow embedding the controller must delete the header or use ALLOW-FROM semantics, otherwise the embed iframe remains blocked when a default SAMEORIGIN/DENY is set.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects direct retriever but code enqueues job
findings.body: File spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 40-45 expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve on a cache miss, while app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15 does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). The test does not verify actual behavior and would fail/pass for the wrong reason, leaving the enqueue path, user_id propagation, and loading render untested.
